text:
cheng: Quick sync — thinking through the ingest stability contract for the new onboarding heuristics. want a short thread to capture tradeoffs.
neha: +1. main pain is flaky smoke vs full bench mismatch. we keep seeing models pass the quick smoke but fail extended latency / memory sweeps.
sam: the smoke currently does 50 samples w/ cold kv-cache. Full bench is 5k samples w/ warm caches. is that disparity intentional?
lisa: it was intentional for speed, but I think we underestimated cache effects. for quantized models warm cache changes latency distribution a lot.
cheng: proposal: add a small warm-cache probe into smoke (e.g., 20 warm samples) and a deterministic trace for one long tail-case. keeps smoke <30s but catches cache regressions.
neha: sounds reasonable. question: how do we avoid increasing cost for every onboarding run? we have thousands of model candidates.
sam: maybe gate warm-cache probe behind "high risk" heuristics: new architecture, quantized artifact, or if model exceeds token-length threshold. default remains cold-only for low-risk variants.
lisa: also add a cheap stability metric: tail90_latency_ratio = p90/p50. if > 3 we fail fast and run full bench. that avoids running full bench for harmless jitter.
cheng: agree. also need explicit tolerances for memory spike regressions. suggestion: memory_regression_pct = (observed_peak - baseline_peak) / baseline_peak. fail if > 15%.
neha: baseline_peak — which baseline? current production model or the model's own initial warmup? we should use the model's declared baseline artifact in the intake metadata.
sam: intake metadata exists but often missing. alternative: fallback baseline = median of last 3 runs for same model family, else run small baseline sweep.
lisa: ops concern: if we start auto-failing on tail metrics, we need a clear remediation path in console: reason, repro command, and quick-link to run full bench on dedicated infra.
cheng: good point. console should show the failing trace and a one-click "rebench" on dedicated pool (costs charged to team). admit-bot: new rule created: "warm_probe_on_smoke" flagged for models with tag:quantized or tag:arch-change. created as draft rule id WPO-2026-03.
neha: we also need to think about dataset sampling bias. bench inputs skew to short prompts. add stratified sampling: 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long, with tokens distribution recorded.
sam: agree — and record per-stratum metrics (latency, mem, quality) so rollouts can weight regressions by expected traffic distribution.
lisa: API/contract changes: the onboarding API needs optional fields: sample_seed, stratification_profile, and expected_traffic_weights. keep defaults but let teams opt into custom profiles.
cheng: backward compatibility: default behavior should preserve existing benches. new fields optional. when omitted, smoke uses current profile but warm_probe rules may still fire.
neha: one more: how long to retain bench traces? we should keep 30 days at full fidelity, 1 year aggregated. opsbot: telemetry retention set to 30d full, 365d aggregated for eng-ml by policy ENGML-TR-7.
sam: QA checklist for rollout: (1) add warm_probe toggle in smoke config, (2) implement tail90_ratio check + 15% mem threshold, (3) stratified sampler, (4) console rebench workflow, (5) docs + changelog.
lisa: estimate effort? small PRs across bench harness + intake proto + console link — ~2 sprint effort if we parallelize.
cheng: I'll draft a short RFC for the follow-up: include config snippets and examples. starting config stub in thread: ```json
{
  "smoke": { "samples": 70, "warm_probe": { "enabled": true, "warm_samples": 20 } },
  "stability": { "tail90_ratio_threshold": 3.0, "mem_regression_pct": 15 }
}
```
neha: nice. add example for stratified sampler too. I'll pick this up to write the intake proto change.
sam: I'll own console repro/playback and rebench link.
lisa: I'll update docs and QA checklist.
cheng: thanks — let's reconvene after RFC draft. :thumbsup:
